questions.q: For a chemical reaction at $300 \text{ K}$, the standard enthalpy change ($\Delta H^{\circ}$) is $-20 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and the standard entropy change ($\Delta S^{\circ}$) is $-50 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$. What is the value of the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^{\circ}$) for the reaction, and what does it imply about the equilibrium constant ($K$)?
questions.solution:
First, calculate the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^{\circ}$) using the equation:
$\Delta G^{\circ} = \Delta H^{\circ} - T\Delta S^{\circ}$

Given:
$\Delta H^{\circ} = -20 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = -20000 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta S^{\circ} = -50 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$
$T = 300 \text{ K}$

Substituting the values:
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -20000 \text{ J mol}^{-1} - (300 \text{ K})(-50 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1})$
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -20000 \text{ J mol}^{-1} + 15000 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -5000 \text{ J mol}^{-1} = -5 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Next, relate $\Delta G^{\circ}$ to the equilibrium constant ($K$) using the equation:
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -RT \ln K$

Since $\Delta G^{\circ}$ is negative ($-5 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), the term $-RT \ln K$ must be negative. This implies that $\ln K$ must be positive ($\ln K > 0$).
For $\ln K > 0$, the equilibrium constant $K$ must be greater than $1$ ($K > 1$).

Answer: $-5 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} \text{ and } K > 1$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the reaction $\text{CO (g)} + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{ (g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{ (g)}$ at $300$ K, given $\Delta U^{\ominus} = -280.0$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $\Delta S^{\ominus} = -86.0$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, the reaction is spontaneous.

Reason (R): For this reaction, $\Delta H^{\ominus}$ is more negative than $\Delta U^{\ominus}$, and the magnitude of $\Delta H^{\ominus}$ is greater than the magnitude of $T\Delta S^{\ominus}$, making $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ negative.

(Given : $R = 8.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
First, evaluate the Assertion (A) by calculating the thermodynamic parameters.
The change in gaseous moles for the reaction is:
$\Delta n_g = n_p - n_r = 1 - \left(1 + 0.5\right) = -0.5$

Calculate $\Delta H^{\ominus}$ at $300$ K:
$\Delta H^{\ominus} = \Delta U^{\ominus} + \Delta n_g R T$
$\Delta H^{\ominus} = -280.0 + (-0.5) \times (8.3 \times 10^{-3}) \times 300$
$\Delta H^{\ominus} = -280.0 - 1.245 = -281.245 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Calculate the entropy term $T\Delta S^{\ominus}$:
$T\Delta S^{\ominus} = 300 \times (-86.0 \times 10^{-3}) = -25.8 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Calculate $\Delta G^{\ominus}$:
$\Delta G^{\ominus} = \Delta H^{\ominus} - T\Delta S^{\ominus}$
$\Delta G^{\ominus} = -281.245 - (-25.8) = -255.445 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Since $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ is negative, the reaction is spontaneous. Thus, Assertion (A) is correct.

Now evaluate the Reason (R):
$\Delta H^{\ominus}$ ($-281.245$ kJ mol$^{-1}$) is indeed more negative than $\Delta U^{\ominus}$ ($-280.0$ kJ mol$^{-1}$).
The magnitude of $\Delta H^{\ominus}$ ($281.245$) is greater than the magnitude of $T\Delta S^{\ominus}$ ($25.8$).
Because the highly favorable (negative) enthalpy change overcomes the unfavorable (negative) entropy change, $\Delta G^{\ominus}$ remains negative. Thus, Reason (R) is correct and is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Given $\Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l)) = -286 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{OH}^-(aq)) = -230 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, the standard enthalpy of neutralization of a strong acid and strong base is $-56 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
Reason (R): The standard enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{H}^+(aq)$ is taken as zero by convention.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
The net ionic equation for the neutralization of a strong acid and a strong base is:
$\mathrm{H}^+(aq) + \mathrm{OH}^-(aq) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l)$

The standard enthalpy of neutralization is calculated using Hess's Law:
$\Delta H_{neut}^\circ = \Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l)) - [\Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{H}^+(aq)) + \Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{OH}^-(aq))]$

By IUPAC convention, the standard enthalpy of formation of the aqueous hydrogen ion, $\mathrm{H}^+(aq)$, is assigned a value of zero at all temperatures. Thus, the Reason is true.

Substituting the given values:
$\Delta H_{neut}^\circ = -286 - [0 + (-230)] = -286 + 230 = -56 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

The Assertion is true, and the calculation explicitly relies on the convention stated in the Reason. Therefore, the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An ideal gas undergoes a thermodynamic process in which it exchanges no heat with its surroundings and performs no work. Which of the following correctly identifies the process and the corresponding change in temperature of the gas?
questions.solution:
Given that the gas exchanges no heat with the surroundings, $q = 0$, which means the process is adiabatic.

Since the gas performs no work, $w = 0$. This condition is satisfied during free expansion (expansion against zero external pressure).

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + w$. Substituting the values, we get $\Delta U = 0 + 0 = 0$.

For an ideal gas, the internal energy is a function of temperature only ($\Delta U = nC_{v}\Delta T$). Therefore, $\Delta U = 0$ implies that $\Delta T = 0$.

Thus, the process is an adiabatic free expansion with $\Delta T = 0$.

Answer: Adiabatic free expansion, $\Delta T = 0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A certain amount of an ideal gas undergoes an isothermal reversible compression. If $1200 \text{ J}$ of work is done on the gas during this process, what are the values of heat exchanged ($q$) and the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) respectively?
questions.solution:
For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant ($\Delta T = 0$). Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta U = 0$).

According to the first law of thermodynamics:
$\Delta U = q + w$

We are given that $1200 \text{ J}$ of work is done on the gas. By IUPAC sign convention, work done on the system is taken as positive, so $w = +1200 \text{ J}$.

Substituting the values into the first law equation:
$0 = q + 1200$
$q = -1200 \text{ J}$

The negative sign indicates that $1200 \text{ J}$ of heat is released by the gas to the surroundings.

Answer: $q = -1200 \text{ J}$, $\Delta U = 0 \text{ J}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If $C_P$ and $C_V$ represent the total heat capacities at constant pressure and constant volume respectively for $n$ moles of an ideal gas, which of the following relationships is correct?
questions.solution:
For $1$ mole of an ideal gas, the molar heat capacities are related by Mayer's relation: $C_{p,m} - C_{v,m} = R$.

For $n$ moles of the gas, the total (extensive) heat capacity at constant pressure is $C_P = nC_{p,m}$ and at constant volume is $C_V = nC_{v,m}$.

Substituting these into the relation gives:
$\dfrac{C_P}{n} - \dfrac{C_V}{n} = R$

Multiplying the entire equation by $n$, we get:
$C_P - C_V = nR$

Answer: $C_P - C_V = nR$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the value of $(\Delta H - \Delta U)$ for the complete combustion of liquid benzene at $298 \text{ K}$?
(Given: $R = 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the complete combustion of liquid benzene at $298 \text{ K}$ is:
$\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_6(\mathrm{l}) + \dfrac{15}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 6\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$

The change in the number of gaseous moles ($\Delta n_g$) is:
$\Delta n_g = n_p(\mathrm{g}) - n_r(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta n_g = 6 - \dfrac{15}{2} = -1.5$

The relationship between enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and internal energy change ($\Delta U$) is:
$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$
$\Delta H - \Delta U = \Delta n_g RT$

Substituting the values:
$\Delta H - \Delta U = -1.5 \times 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{mol}^{-1} \times 298 \text{ K}$
$\Delta H - \Delta U = -3716.358 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta H - \Delta U \approx -3.716 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Treating $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ as a gas incorrectly leads to $\Delta n_g = +1.5$, giving $+3.716 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Treating both $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_6$ and $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ as gases incorrectly leads to $\Delta n_g = +0.5$, giving $+1.239 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Treating $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_6$ as a gas but $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ as a liquid incorrectly gives $\Delta n_g = -2.5$, leading to $-6.194 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $-3.716 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a reversible Carnot cycle, the magnitude of the net work done by the gas is equal to the heat absorbed during the isothermal expansion.

Reason (R): In a reversible Carnot cycle, the work done during the adiabatic expansion is exactly equal and opposite to the work done during the adiabatic compression.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false: According to the Second Law of Thermodynamics, no heat engine can have 100% efficiency. In a Carnot cycle, some heat ($q_{out}$) must be rejected during the isothermal compression. Therefore, the magnitude of the net work done ($|w_{net}| = q_{in} - q_{out}$) is strictly less than the heat absorbed ($q_{in}$) during the isothermal expansion.

Reason (R) is true: For an ideal gas, the internal energy change depends only on temperature ($\Delta U = nC_v\Delta T$). In a Carnot cycle operating between temperatures $T_{high}$ and $T_{low}$, the adiabatic expansion goes from $T_{high}$ to $T_{low}$, so $w_{exp} = \Delta U_{exp} = nC_v(T_{low} - T_{high})$. The adiabatic compression goes from $T_{low}$ to $T_{high}$, so $w_{comp} = \Delta U_{comp} = nC_v(T_{high} - T_{low})$. Thus, $w_{exp} = -w_{comp}$, meaning they are exactly equal in magnitude and opposite in sign.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a hypothetical reaction, the standard enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and standard entropy change ($\Delta S$) are $-40 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $-100 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. Under which of the following temperature conditions will the reaction be spontaneous?
questions.solution:
For a reaction to be spontaneous, the change in Gibbs free energy ($\Delta G$) must be negative.

$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0$

Given:
$\Delta H = -40 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = -40000 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta S = -100 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Substituting the values into the inequality:
$-40000 - T(-100) < 0$
$-40000 + 100T < 0$
$100T < 40000$
$T < 400 \text{ K}$

Thus, the reaction will be spontaneous at temperatures less than $400 \text{ K}$.

Answer: $T < 400 \text{ K}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the dimerization of nitrogen dioxide gas into dinitrogen tetroxide gas:
$2\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_{4(\mathrm{g})}$

Which of the following correctly describes the signs of enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and entropy change ($\Delta S$) for this process, and the temperature condition for its spontaneity?
options: $\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S < 0$; spontaneous at high temperatures
$\Delta H > 0$, $\Delta S > 0$; spontaneous at high temperatures
$\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S < 0$; spontaneous at low temperatures
$\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S > 0$; spontaneous at all temperatures
questions.solution:
In the dimerization process, $2\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_{4(\mathrm{g})}$, a new N-N bond is formed without breaking any existing bonds. Bond formation releases energy, so the process is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$).

The number of gaseous moles decreases from 2 to 1 ($\Delta n_g = -1$), which means the randomness of the system decreases, so $\Delta S < 0$.

According to the Gibbs free energy equation, $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$.

For the reaction to be spontaneous, $\Delta G$ must be negative. Since both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ are negative, $\Delta G$ will be negative only when the magnitude of $\Delta H$ is greater than $T\Delta S$, which occurs at low temperatures.

Answer: $\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S < 0$; spontaneous at low temperatures

Which of the following correctly describes the signs of enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and entropy change ($\Delta S$) for this process, and the temperature condition for its spontaneity?
questions.explanation:
In the dimerization process, $2\mathrm{NO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2\mathrm{O}_{4(\mathrm{g})}$, a new N-N bond is formed without breaking any existing bonds. Bond formation releases energy, so the process is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$).

The number of gaseous moles decreases from 2 to 1 ($\Delta n_g = -1$), which means the randomness of the system decreases, so $\Delta S < 0$.

According to the Gibbs free energy equation, $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$.

For the reaction to be spontaneous, $\Delta G$ must be negative. Since both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ are negative, $\Delta G$ will be negative only when the magnitude of $\Delta H$ is greater than $T\Delta S$, which occurs at low temperatures.

Answer: $\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S < 0$; spontaneous at low temperatures

questions.q:
Given the standard enthalpy of reaction for the formation of hydrogen chloride:
$\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g}) \quad \Delta_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{H}^{\circ} = -184.6 \mathrm{~kJ}$

Calculate the enthalpy change when $18.25 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})$ decomposes completely into its constituent elements. (Molar mass of $\mathrm{HCl} = 36.5 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The given reaction is for the formation of $2$ moles of $\mathrm{HCl}$ with $\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{H}^{\circ} = -184.6 \mathrm{~kJ}$.

The decomposition of $2$ moles of $\mathrm{HCl}$ is the reverse reaction, so its enthalpy change is $+184.6 \mathrm{~kJ}$.

First, calculate the number of moles in $18.25 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{HCl}$:
Number of moles $= \dfrac{\text{Given mass}}{\text{Molar mass}} = \dfrac{18.25}{36.5} = 0.5 \mathrm{~mol}$.

Since the decomposition of $2$ moles of $\mathrm{HCl}$ requires $+184.6 \mathrm{~kJ}$, the enthalpy change for the decomposition of $0.5$ moles is:
$\Delta\mathrm{H} = \dfrac{+184.6 \mathrm{~kJ}}{2 \mathrm{~mol}} \times 0.5 \mathrm{~mol} = +46.15 \mathrm{~kJ}$.

Answer: $+46.15 \mathrm{~kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During the isothermal free expansion of an ideal gas, the entropy of the system increases even though no heat is exchanged with the surroundings.

Reason (R): Entropy is a path function, and its change for the system depends on the actual irreversible path taken during the expansion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: In an isothermal free expansion of an ideal gas, the external pressure is zero, so the work done $W = 0$. Since the process is isothermal, the change in internal energy $\Delta U = 0$. According to the first law of thermodynamics, $q = \Delta U - W = 0$. However, because the volume increases, the entropy of the system increases ($\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = nR \ln(V_2/V_1) > 0$).

Reason (R) is false: Entropy is a state function, not a path function. The change in entropy of the system is independent of the actual irreversible path taken. It is calculated using a hypothetical reversible path between the same initial and final states.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false

Assertion (A): For the reaction $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)}$, the value of $\Delta G$ becomes more positive as temperature increases.
Reason (R): The synthesis of ammonia from its elements is an exothermic process.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: For the Haber process, $\Delta n_g = 2 - 4 = -2$. Since the number of gaseous moles decreases, the entropy change is negative ($\Delta S < 0$). According to the Gibbs free energy equation, $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$. Because $\Delta S$ is negative, the term $-T\Delta S$ is positive. As temperature ($T$) increases, the positive contribution of $-T\Delta S$ increases, making $\Delta G$ more positive.

Reason (R) is true: The synthesis of ammonia is an exothermic process ($\Delta H < 0$).

However, the exothermic nature of the reaction explains why it is spontaneous at low temperatures, but it does not explain why $\Delta G$ becomes more positive as temperature increases. The correct explanation for the temperature dependence is the negative entropy change ($\Delta S < 0$). Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

Assertion (A): The entropy change ($\Delta S$) for the combustion of solid magnesium to form solid magnesium oxide is negative.

Reason (R): The reaction involves a decrease in the total number of moles of gaseous species.

options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the combustion of solid magnesium is:
$2\text{Mg}(\text{s}) + \text{O}_{2}(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{MgO}(\text{s})$

In this reaction, the reactants contain $1$ mole of gaseous species ($\text{O}_{2}$), while the products contain $0$ moles of gaseous species. The change in the number of gaseous moles is $\Delta n_{g} = 0 - 1 = -1$.

Because there is a decrease in the number of gaseous moles, the randomness or disorder of the system decreases. Consequently, the entropy change ($\Delta S$) for the reaction is negative.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is true. Reason (R) correctly states that the reaction involves a decrease in the total number of moles of gaseous species, which is the fundamental thermodynamic reason for the negative entropy change. Thus, Reason (R) is true and is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An ideal gas expands isothermally at temperature $T$ from an initial volume $V_1$ to a final volume $V_2$ against a constant external pressure $P_{\text{ext}}$. Which of the following expressions correctly represents the change in entropy of the surroundings ($\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}}$) for this process?
questions.solution:
For an irreversible expansion against a constant external pressure $P_{\text{ext}}$, the work done by the system is given by $W = -P_{\text{ext}}(V_2 - V_1)$.

Since the process is isothermal for an ideal gas, the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta U = 0$).

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q_{\text{sys}} + W$. Therefore, the actual heat absorbed by the system is $q_{\text{sys}} = -W = P_{\text{ext}}(V_2 - V_1)$.

The heat absorbed by the surroundings is the negative of the heat absorbed by the system: $q_{\text{surr}} = -q_{\text{sys}} = -P_{\text{ext}}(V_2 - V_1)$.

The change in entropy of the surroundings is calculated using the actual heat exchanged: $\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = \dfrac{q_{\text{surr}}}{T} = \dfrac{-P_{\text{ext}}(V_2 - V_1)}{T}$.

Note that $\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}}$ is not equal to $-\Delta S_{\text{system}}$ because the process is irreversible.

Answer: $\dfrac{-P_{\text{ext}}(V_2 - V_1)}{T}$

questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Process)List II (Thermodynamic parameters)
A. Isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gasI. $q = 0$, $w > 0$, $\Delta U > 0$
B. Adiabatic compressionII. $w = 0$, $q > 0$, $\Delta U > 0$
C. Heat supplied at constant volumeIII. $q = 0$, $w = 0$, $\Delta U = 0$
D. Free expansion of an ideal gas adiabaticallyIV. $\Delta U = 0$, $q > 0$, $w < 0$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + w$.

A. For isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gas, temperature is constant, so $\Delta U = 0$. Since it is an expansion, work is done by the system ($w < 0$). Therefore, $q = -w > 0$. (Matches IV)

B. For adiabatic compression, there is no heat exchange ($q = 0$). Compression means work is done on the system ($w > 0$). Therefore, $\Delta U = 0 + w > 0$. (Matches I)

C. When heat is supplied at constant volume, the process is isochoric ($\Delta V = 0$), so $w = 0$. Heat supplied means $q > 0$. Therefore, $\Delta U = q + 0 > 0$. (Matches II)

D. For free expansion of an ideal gas, the external pressure is zero, so $w = 0$. Since it is adiabatic, $q = 0$. Therefore, $\Delta U = 0 + 0 = 0$. (Matches III)

The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The standard enthalpies of formation for three hypothetical solid salts (P, Q, and R) and their respective aqueous ions are given in the table below (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$):

Salt$\Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Solid})$$\Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Cation}(aq))$$\Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Anion}(aq))$
P-900-400-400
Q-500-300-250
R-700-350-360

What is the correct order of these salts from the most exothermic to the most endothermic standard enthalpy of solution?
questions.solution:
The standard enthalpy of solution ($\Delta H_{sol}^\circ$) for a salt is calculated using Hess's Law:
$\Delta H_{sol}^\circ = \Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Cation}(aq)) + \Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Anion}(aq)) - \Delta H_f^\circ(\text{Solid})$

Calculating for each salt:
For P: $\Delta H_{sol}^\circ = (-400) + (-400) - (-900) = -800 + 900 = +100 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
For Q: $\Delta H_{sol}^\circ = (-300) + (-250) - (-500) = -550 + 500 = -50 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
For R: $\Delta H_{sol}^\circ = (-350) + (-360) - (-700) = -710 + 700 = -10 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Comparing the values, the order from most exothermic (most negative) to most endothermic (most positive) is Q ($-50$) < R ($-10$) < P ($+100$).

Ranking based solely on the solid enthalpy or the sum of the aqueous ions without subtracting correctly leads to the reverse or incorrect orders.

Answer: Q < R < P

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Reaction)List-II (Relation)
(A) $H_2(g) + Br_2(g) \rightarrow 2HBr(g)$(I) $\Delta H > \Delta U$
(B) $N_2O_4(g) \rightarrow 2NO_2(g)$(II) $\Delta H = \Delta U$
(C) $N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightarrow 2NH_3(g)$(III) $\Delta H < \Delta U$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The relationship between enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and internal energy change ($\Delta U$) is given by $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$.

For reaction (A): $H_2(g) + Br_2(g) \rightarrow 2HBr(g)$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0$. Therefore, $\Delta H = \Delta U$. (A matches II)

For reaction (B): $N_2O_4(g) \rightarrow 2NO_2(g)$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = 1$. Since $\Delta n_g > 0$, $\Delta H > \Delta U$. (B matches I)

For reaction (C): $N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightarrow 2NH_3(g)$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$. Since $\Delta n_g < 0$, $\Delta H < \Delta U$. (C matches III).

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a reversible reaction $\text{X} \rightleftharpoons \text{Y}$, the standard enthalpy change ($\Delta H^\circ$) is $400$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and the standard entropy change ($\Delta S^\circ$) is $800$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$. Assuming $\Delta H^\circ$ and $\Delta S^\circ$ are independent of temperature, the temperature in $^\circ\text{C}$ at which the equilibrium mixture contains equal moles of $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ is:
questions.solution:
For the reaction $\text{X} \rightleftharpoons \text{Y}$, the equilibrium constant is $K = \dfrac{[\text{Y}]}{[\text{X}]}$.

When the equilibrium mixture contains equal moles of $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$, their concentrations are equal, meaning $K = 1$.

The standard Gibbs free energy change is given by $\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K$. For $K = 1$, $\Delta G^\circ = 0$.

Using the Gibbs-Helmholtz equation $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T \Delta S^\circ$, we have:
$\Delta H^\circ = T \Delta S^\circ$

Given $\Delta H^\circ = 400$ kJ mol$^{-1} = 400000$ J mol$^{-1}$ and $\Delta S^\circ = 800$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.

Solving for temperature $T$ in Kelvin:
$T = \dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{\Delta S^\circ} = \dfrac{400000}{800} = 500$ K

Converting the temperature to Celsius:
$T (\text{in } ^\circ\text{C}) = 500 - 273 = 227$ $^\circ\text{C}$

Answer: $227$

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When an ideal gas undergoes adiabatic expansion, its internal energy decreases.

Reason (R): According to IUPAC sign convention, the work done by a system during expansion is taken as negative ($w < 0$).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: In an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange ($q = 0$). During expansion, work is done by the system, so $w < 0$. According to the first law of thermodynamics ($\Delta U = q + w$), $\Delta U = 0 + w$. Since $w$ is negative, $\Delta U$ is negative, meaning the internal energy decreases.

Reason (R) is true: By IUPAC convention in chemistry, work done by the system (expansion) is taken as negative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the reaction $2\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})$, the heat of reaction at constant volume is $-221.0 \text{ kJ}$ at $300 \text{ K}$. The heat of reaction at constant pressure at the same temperature is:
(Given $R = \dfrac{25}{3} \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
From the First Law of Thermodynamics, heat absorbed at constant volume ($q_v$) is equal to the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$), and heat absorbed at constant pressure ($q_p$) is equal to the change in enthalpy ($\Delta H$).

Given:
$q_v = \Delta U = -221.0 \text{ kJ}$
$T = 300 \text{ K}$
$R = \dfrac{25}{3} \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

For the reaction $2\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})$:
$\Delta n_g = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = 1$ (Solid carbon is not counted).

The relationship between $q_p$ and $q_v$ is:
$q_p = q_v + \Delta n_g RT$

First, calculate the $\Delta n_g RT$ term in kJ:
$\Delta n_g RT = 1 \times \left(\dfrac{25}{3}\right) \times 300 \text{ J}$
$= 2500 \text{ J} = 2.5 \text{ kJ}$

Now, substitute the values:
$q_p = -221.0 \text{ kJ} + 2.5 \text{ kJ}$
$q_p = -218.5 \text{ kJ}$

Note: A common mistake is to include the solid reactant in the $\Delta n_g$ calculation (giving $\Delta n_g = -1$ and an incorrect answer of $-223.5 \text{ kJ}$) or failing to convert the $RT$ term to kJ (giving $+2279 \text{ kJ}$).

Answer: $-218.5 \text{ kJ}$

(A) Isothermal reversible expansion(I) $\Delta S_{\text{total}} > 0$
(B) Isothermal irreversible expansion(II) $w = 0$
(C) Adiabatic reversible expansion(III) $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = 0$
(D) Isothermal free expansion(IV) $q = 0$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For any reversible process, the total entropy change of the universe is zero, so $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = 0$ for isothermal reversible expansion (A $\rightarrow$ III).

In an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange with the surroundings, so $q = 0$ (C $\rightarrow$ IV).

During free expansion, the gas expands against zero external pressure ($P_{\text{ext}} = 0$), so the work done $w = 0$ (D $\rightarrow$ II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.q:
An ideal gas at $400\text{ K}$ expands isothermally from $1.0\text{ L}$ to $4.0\text{ L}$ against a constant external pressure of $2.0\text{ bar}$. The heat absorbed ($q$) by the gas in this process is:

(Given: $1\text{ L bar} = 100\text{ J}$)
questions.solution:
The work done by the gas against a constant external pressure is:
$W = -P_{\text{ext}}(V_{f} - V_{i})$

$W = -2.0 \times (4.0 - 1.0) = -6.0\text{ L bar}$

Converting to Joules:
$W = -6.0 \times 100 = -600\text{ J}$

For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta U = 0$).

According to the first law of thermodynamics:
$\Delta U = q + W$

$0 = q + (-600)$

$q = +600\text{ J}$

Thus, the heat absorbed by the gas is $+600\text{ J}$.

Answer: $+600\text{ J}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate is given by the following equation:
$\text{CaCO}_3\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{CaO(s)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$
At $1000$ K, the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^{\ominus}$) for this reaction is $+22.6$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and the standard entropy change ($\Delta S^{\ominus}$) is $+160$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.
What is the standard internal energy change ($\Delta U^{\ominus}$) for the reaction at $1000$ K?
(Given: $R = 8.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
First, calculate the standard enthalpy change ($\Delta H^{\ominus}$) using the Gibbs free energy equation:

$\Delta G^{\ominus} = \Delta H^{\ominus} - T \Delta S^{\ominus}$

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = \Delta G^{\ominus} + T \Delta S^{\ominus}$

Substituting the given values (converting $\Delta S^{\ominus}$ to kJ K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$):

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = 22.6 + 1000 \times (160 \times 10^{-3})$

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = 22.6 + 160 = +182.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Next, determine the change in the number of moles of gaseous species ($\Delta n_g$). Only $\text{CO}_2$ is gaseous:

$\Delta n_g = 1 - 0 = 1$

Now, calculate the standard internal energy change ($\Delta U^{\ominus}$) using the relation:

$\Delta H^{\ominus} = \Delta U^{\ominus} + \Delta n_g R T$

$\Delta U^{\ominus} = \Delta H^{\ominus} - \Delta n_g R T$

$\Delta U^{\ominus} = 182.6 - (1) \times (8.3 \times 10^{-3}) \times 1000$

$\Delta U^{\ominus} = 182.6 - 8.3 = +174.3 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $+174.3$ kJ mol$^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The variation of standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^\circ$) with temperature ($T$) for a reversible reaction is represented by a straight line. The line intersects the $\Delta G^\circ$ axis (y-axis) at $+40$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and the temperature axis (x-axis) at $500$ K. Assuming standard enthalpy ($\Delta H^\circ$) and standard entropy ($\Delta S^\circ$) changes are independent of temperature, the value of the equilibrium constant $K$ at $500$ K and the standard entropy change $\Delta S^\circ$ (in J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$) respectively are:
questions.solution:
The relationship between standard Gibbs free energy change, enthalpy change, and entropy change is given by the Gibbs-Helmholtz equation:

$\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$

This is the equation of a straight line ($y = mx + c$), where $y = \Delta G^\circ$, $x = T$, slope $m = -\Delta S^\circ$, and y-intercept $c = \Delta H^\circ$.

From the given information, the y-intercept is $+40$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. Therefore, $\Delta H^\circ = 40$ kJ mol$^{-1} = 40000$ J mol$^{-1}$.

The line intersects the temperature axis at $500$ K, which means at $T = 500$ K, $\Delta G^\circ = 0$.

Using the relation $\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K$, when $\Delta G^\circ = 0$, we have $-RT \ln K = 0 \Rightarrow \ln K = 0 \Rightarrow K = 1$.

Substituting $\Delta G^\circ = 0$ and $T = 500$ K into the Gibbs-Helmholtz equation:

$0 = \Delta H^\circ - (500)\Delta S^\circ$

$\Delta S^\circ = \dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{500} = \dfrac{40000}{500} = 80$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.

Thus, $K = 1$ and $\Delta S^\circ = 80$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.

Answer: $1$ and $80$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
One mole of an ideal gas undergoes a reversible Carnot cycle consisting of four steps: isothermal expansion (from $V_1$ to $V_2$ at $T_{\text{high}}$), adiabatic expansion (to $V_3$ at $T_{\text{low}}$), isothermal compression (to $V_4$ at $T_{\text{low}}$), and adiabatic compression (back to $V_1$ at $T_{\text{high}}$).

Match the thermodynamic quantities in List-I with their expressions in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Work done in adiabatic expansion(I) Zero
(B) Heat exchanged in isothermal compression(II) $C_v(T_{\text{low}} - T_{\text{high}})$
(C) Net internal energy change for the cycle(III) $-RT_{\text{low}} \ln\left(\dfrac{V_4}{V_3}\right)$
(D) Sum of work done in the two adiabatic steps(IV) $RT_{\text{low}} \ln\left(\dfrac{V_4}{V_3}\right)$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to the IUPAC sign convention, the first law of thermodynamics is $\Delta U = q + w$.

For the adiabatic expansion from $T_{\text{high}}$ to $T_{\text{low}}$:
$q = 0$, so $w = \Delta U = C_v(T_{\text{low}} - T_{\text{high}})$. Thus, (A) matches (II).

For the isothermal compression from $V_3$ to $V_4$ at $T_{\text{low}}$:
The change in internal energy $\Delta U = 0$.
Work done $w = -RT_{\text{low}} \ln\left(\dfrac{V_4}{V_3}\right)$.
Heat exchanged $q = \Delta U - w = RT_{\text{low}} \ln\left(\dfrac{V_4}{V_3}\right)$. Thus, (B) matches (IV).

For any complete cyclic process, internal energy is a state function, so the net change $\Delta U_{\text{cycle}} = 0$. Thus, (C) matches (I).

The sum of work done in the two adiabatic steps is the sum of their internal energy changes:
$w_{\text{adiab}} = C_v(T_{\text{low}} - T_{\text{high}}) + C_v(T_{\text{high}} - T_{\text{low}}) = 0$. Thus, (D) matches (I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(I)

Match List-I with List-II for the thermodynamic processes of an ideal gas.

questions.solution:
(A) Adiabatic free expansion: Heat exchange is zero ($q = 0$). Expansion against zero external pressure means work done is zero ($w = 0$). By the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + w = 0$.

(B) Reversible adiabatic expansion: Heat exchange is zero ($q = 0$). During expansion, work is done by the gas ($w < 0$). Thus, $\Delta U = w < 0$.

(C) Reversible isothermal expansion: Temperature is constant, so for an ideal gas $\Delta U = 0$. Work is done by the gas ($w < 0$), so $q = -w > 0$.

(D) Isochoric heating: Volume is constant, so work done is zero ($w = 0$). Heat is absorbed to increase temperature ($q > 0$). Thus, $\Delta U = q > 0$.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which of the following physical processes is the change in entropy ($\Delta S$) positive?
options: Crystallization of sugar from a supersaturated solution
Condensation of steam to liquid water
questions.solution:
Entropy is a measure of the degree of randomness or disorder in a system.

When solid $\text{NaCl}$ dissolves in water, the highly ordered crystal lattice breaks down into free-moving $\text{Na}^{+}$ and $\text{Cl}^{-}$ ions in the solution, which increases the randomness. Hence, $\Delta S > 0$.

For the dissolution of $\text{CO}_{2}$ gas in water, the gaseous molecules are confined to the liquid phase, decreasing randomness ($\Delta S < 0$).

Crystallization of sugar involves the formation of an ordered solid from a solution, decreasing randomness ($\Delta S < 0$).

Condensation of steam converts a gas into a liquid, which also decreases randomness ($\Delta S < 0$).

Answer: Dissolution of solid $\text{NaCl}$ in water

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During the isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, its internal energy increases.
Reason (R): The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on its temperature and is independent of its pressure and volume.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
For an ideal gas, there are no intermolecular forces of attraction. Hence, its internal energy is entirely kinetic and depends only on its absolute temperature. It is independent of pressure and volume. Thus, Reason (R) is true.

During an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant ($\Delta T = 0$). Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) must be zero. Therefore, the internal energy remains constant during isothermal expansion, making Assertion (A) false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

questions.q:
One mole of an ideal gas undergoes a 3-step cyclic process as follows:
(i) Isochoric heating from temperature $T_1$ to $T_2$ at volume $V_1$.
(ii) Isothermal expansion at temperature $T_2$ from volume $V_1$ to $V_2$.
(iii) Isobaric compression from volume $V_2$ back to $V_1$ at pressure $P_1$ (returning the gas to temperature $T_1$).

Which of the following expressions represents the net thermodynamic work ($w$) for the complete cycle? (Assume IUPAC sign convention)
questions.solution:
According to the IUPAC sign convention, work done is given by $w = -\int P dV$.

Step (i) Isochoric heating: Since volume is constant ($V_1$), $\Delta V = 0$.
Work done, $w_1 = 0$

Step (ii) Isothermal expansion: The gas expands from $V_1$ to $V_2$ at constant temperature $T_2$.
Work done, $w_2 = -nRT_2 \ln\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right) = -RT_2 \ln\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$ (since $n = 1$)

Step (iii) Isobaric compression: The gas is compressed from $V_2$ to $V_1$ at constant pressure $P_1$.
Work done, $w_3 = -P_1(V_1 - V_2) = -P_1 V_1 + P_1 V_2$
Using the ideal gas equation for states 1 and 3: $P_1 V_1 = RT_1$ and $P_1 V_2 = RT_2$.
Substituting these values, $w_3 = -RT_1 + RT_2 = R(T_2 - T_1)$

The net work done in the complete cycle is the sum of the work done in each step:
$w_{net} = w_1 + w_2 + w_3 = 0 - RT_2 \ln\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right) + R(T_2 - T_1)$

Therefore, $w_{net} = -RT_2 \ln\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right) + R(T_2 - T_1)$

Answer: $-RT_2 \ln\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right) + R(T_2 - T_1)$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During the adiabatic free expansion of an ideal gas, the temperature of the gas decreases.

Reason (R): In free expansion, the gas expands against zero external pressure doing no work, and since the process is adiabatic, the internal energy remains constant.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is incorrect. For the adiabatic free expansion of an ideal gas, the temperature remains constant ($\Delta T = 0$), it does not decrease.

Reason (R) is correct. Free expansion means expansion against vacuum ($P_{\text{ext}} = 0$), so work done $w = 0$. Since the process is adiabatic, heat exchange $q = 0$. According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + w = 0$. For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature, so $\Delta T = 0$.

Answer: Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For which of the following reactions is the change in enthalpy ($\Delta \text{H}$) equal to the change in internal energy ($\Delta \text{U}$) at a given constant temperature?
questions.solution:
The relationship between change in enthalpy ($\Delta \text{H}$) and change in internal energy ($\Delta \text{U}$) is given by:
$\Delta \text{H} = \Delta \text{U} + \Delta \text{n}_\text{g}\text{RT}$

For $\Delta \text{H} = \Delta \text{U}$, the term $\Delta \text{n}_\text{g}\text{RT}$ must be equal to zero. Since $\text{R}$ and $\text{T}$ are non-zero, this requires $\Delta \text{n}_\text{g} = 0$.

$\Delta \text{n}_\text{g}$ is the difference between the number of moles of gaseous products and gaseous reactants.

Let us evaluate $\Delta \text{n}_\text{g}$ for each option:
Option 1: $\Delta \text{n}_\text{g} = (1 + 1) - 1 = 1$
Option 2: $\Delta \text{n}_\text{g} = 2 - (2 + 1) = -1$
Option 3: $\Delta \text{n}_\text{g} = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0$
Option 4: $\Delta \text{n}_\text{g} = 2 - 1 = 1$ (Note: $\text{I}_2$ is in the solid state, so it is not counted in $\Delta \text{n}_\text{g}$, even though the total number of moles of all substances does not change).

Therefore, the reaction $\text{H}_2(\text{g}) + \text{Cl}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{HCl}(\text{g})$ satisfies the condition $\Delta \text{H} = \Delta \text{U}$.

Answer: $\text{H}_2(\text{g}) + \text{Cl}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{HCl}(\text{g})$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For one mole of an ideal gas, the molar heat capacity at constant volume ($C_v$) is greater than the molar heat capacity at constant pressure ($C_p$) by an amount $R$.
Reason (R): Heating a gas at constant pressure requires additional heat to do work of expansion against the external pressure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because for an ideal gas, the molar heat capacity at constant pressure ($C_p$) is greater than the molar heat capacity at constant volume ($C_v$) by the universal gas constant $R$ (i.e., $C_p - C_v = R$, not $C_v - C_p = R$).

Reason (R) is true. When a gas is heated at constant volume, no expansion work is done, and all the heat supplied increases the internal energy. However, when heated at constant pressure, the gas expands and does work against the external pressure. Therefore, extra heat must be supplied to achieve the same rise in temperature, which is the physical reason why $C_p > C_v$.

Thus, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the thermochemical equation for the synthesis of ammonia:
$\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g}) \quad \Delta_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{H}^{\circ} = -92.4 \mathrm{~kJ}$

What is the standard enthalpy change for the decomposition of one mole of ammonia gas into its constituent elements?
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the formation of $2$ moles of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ with $\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{H}^{\circ} = -92.4 \mathrm{~kJ}$.

The decomposition of ammonia is the reverse reaction:
$2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g})$
For this reverse reaction, the sign of the enthalpy change is reversed:
$\Delta\mathrm{H}^{\circ} = +92.4 \mathrm{~kJ}$ for the decomposition of $2$ moles of $\mathrm{NH}_3$.

For the decomposition of $1$ mole of $\mathrm{NH}_3$, the enthalpy change is:
$\Delta\mathrm{H}^{\circ} = \dfrac{+92.4}{2} = +46.2 \mathrm{~kJ}$.

Answer: $+46.2 \mathrm{~kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The freezing of liquid water to solid ice is a spontaneous process at $263\text{ K}$.
Reason (R): For the freezing of water, both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ are negative, and at $263\text{ K}$, the magnitude of enthalpy change is less than the magnitude of $T\Delta S$ ($|\Delta H| < |T\Delta S|$).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: The freezing point of water is $273\text{ K}$. At any temperature below $273\text{ K}$ (such as $263\text{ K}$), the freezing of liquid water into solid ice is a spontaneous process.

Reason (R) is incorrect: During the freezing of water, heat is released (exothermic, $\Delta H < 0$) and the randomness decreases as liquid turns to solid ($\Delta S < 0$). For the process to be spontaneous, the Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$) must be negative.

Since both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ are negative, we can write $\Delta G = -|\Delta H| + T|\Delta S|$. For $\Delta G$ to be negative, the magnitude of the enthalpy term must be greater than the magnitude of the entropy term, i.e., $|\Delta H| > |T\Delta S|$. The Reason incorrectly states that $|\Delta H| < |T\Delta S|$.

Therefore, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$2\text{ mol}$ of an ideal gas at $300\text{ K}$ expands isothermally into a vacuum, increasing its volume from $5\text{ L}$ to $10\text{ L}$. What are the values of work done ($W$) and change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) for this process?

(Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, $\ln 2 = 0.693$)
questions.solution:
Expansion of a gas into a vacuum is known as free expansion. In a vacuum, the external pressure ($P_{\text{ext}}$) is zero.

The work done against a constant external pressure is given by $W = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V$. Since $P_{\text{ext}} = 0$, the work done $W = 0$.

For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant ($\Delta T = 0$). The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, so the change in internal energy $\Delta U = 0$.

Answer: $W = 0$, $\Delta U = 0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two moles of an ideal gas undergo reversible isothermal expansion from a volume of $10 \text{ L}$ to $100 \text{ L}$ at $300 \text{ K}$. What is the amount of heat absorbed by the gas in this process?
(Given: $R = 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300 \approx 5744 \text{ J}$)
questions.solution:
For an isothermal process involving an ideal gas, the temperature remains constant, so the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta U = 0$).

According to the First Law of Thermodynamics:
$\Delta U = q + W$
$0 = q + W \Rightarrow q = -W$

The work done during reversible isothermal expansion is calculated as:
$W = -2.303 nRT \log\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$

Substituting the given values ($n = 2 \text{ moles}$, $V_1 = 10 \text{ L}$, $V_2 = 100 \text{ L}$):
$W = -2.303 \times 2 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \log\left(\dfrac{100}{10}\right)$
$W = -2 \times (2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300) \times \log(10)$
$W = -2 \times 5744 \times 1$
$W = -11488 \text{ J} = -11.488 \text{ kJ} \approx -11.49 \text{ kJ}$

The negative sign indicates that work is done by the gas during expansion.

Since $q = -W$, the heat absorbed by the gas is:
$q = -(-11.49 \text{ kJ}) = +11.49 \text{ kJ}$

Answer: $+11.49 \text{ kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following gas-phase dissociation reaction:
$\text{X (g)} \rightarrow \text{Y (g)} + \text{Z (g)}$
Given $\Delta U^{\ominus} = 83.35$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $\Delta S^{\ominus} = 175$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.
Assuming $\Delta U^{\ominus}$ and $\Delta S^{\ominus}$ are independent of temperature, calculate the temperature above which the reaction becomes spontaneous.
(Given : $R = 8.3$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
For a reaction to be spontaneous, the standard Gibbs free energy change must be negative ($\Delta G^{\ominus} < 0$).

$\Delta G^{\ominus} = \Delta H^{\ominus} - T \Delta S^{\ominus} < 0$

The standard enthalpy change $\Delta H^{\ominus}$ is related to $\Delta U^{\ominus}$ by:
$\Delta H^{\ominus} = \Delta U^{\ominus} + \Delta n_g R T$

Substituting this into the Gibbs equation gives:
$\Delta U^{\ominus} + \Delta n_g R T - T \Delta S^{\ominus} < 0$

Rearranging for $T$:
$\Delta U^{\ominus} < T (\Delta S^{\ominus} - \Delta n_g R)$
$T > \dfrac{\Delta U^{\ominus}}{\Delta S^{\ominus} - \Delta n_g R}$

For the given reaction $\text{X (g)} \rightarrow \text{Y (g)} + \text{Z (g)}$, the change in gaseous moles is:
$\Delta n_g = (1 + 1) - 1 = 1$

Now, calculate the denominator term (ensure units are consistent, converting J to kJ):
$\Delta S^{\ominus} - \Delta n_g R = 175 - (1 \times 8.3) = 166.7 \text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1} = 0.1667 \text{ kJ K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$

Calculate the threshold temperature $T$:
$T = \dfrac{83.35}{0.1667} = 500 \text{ K}$

Therefore, the reaction becomes spontaneous above $500$ K.

Answer: $500$ K

$\Delta U^{\ominus} < T (\Delta S^{\ominus} - \Delta n_g R)$
$T > \dfrac{\Delta U^{\ominus}}{\Delta S^{\ominus} - \Delta n_g R}$

For the given reaction $\text{X (g)} \rightarrow \text{Y (g)} + \text{Z (g)}$, the change in gaseous moles is:
$\Delta n_g = (1 + 1) - 1 = 1$

Now, calculate the denominator term (ensure units are consistent, converting J to kJ):
$\Delta S^{\ominus} - \Delta n_g R = 175 - (1 \times 8.3) = 166.7 \text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1} = 0.1667 \text{ kJ K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$

Calculate the threshold temperature $T$:
$T = \dfrac{83.35}{0.1667} = 500 \text{ K}$

Therefore, the reaction becomes spontaneous above $500$ K.

Answer: $500$ K

(B) $\text{I}_{2}\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{I}_{2}\text{(g)}$(II) $\Delta S < 0$, $\Delta n_{g} < 0$
(C) $\text{N}_{2}\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_{3}\text{(g)}$(III) $\Delta S > 0$, physical change
(D) $\text{PCl}_{5}\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{PCl}_{3}\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_{2}\text{(g)}$(IV) $\Delta S < 0$, physical change

questions.solution:
(A) $\text{H}_{2}\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{H}_{2}\text{O(s)}$ represents the freezing of water. It is a physical change where a less ordered liquid converts into a highly ordered solid, so $\Delta S < 0$. Thus, (A) matches (IV).

(B) $\text{I}_{2}\text{(s)} \rightarrow \text{I}_{2}\text{(g)}$ represents the sublimation of iodine. It is a physical change where a solid converts into a highly disordered gas, so $\Delta S > 0$. Thus, (B) matches (III).

(C) $\text{N}_{2}\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_{3}\text{(g)}$ is a chemical reaction. The change in the number of moles of gas is $\Delta n_{g} = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$. Since $\Delta n_{g} < 0$, the randomness decreases, so $\Delta S < 0$. Thus, (C) matches (II).

(D) $\text{PCl}_{5}\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{PCl}_{3}\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_{2}\text{(g)}$ is a chemical reaction. The change in the number of moles of gas is $\Delta n_{g} = (1 + 1) - 1 = +1$. Since $\Delta n_{g} > 0$, the randomness increases, so $\Delta S > 0$. Thus, (D) matches (I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider an ideal gas undergoing a reversible Carnot cycle. Read the following statements regarding the entropy changes during the processes:

Statement I: The total entropy change of the universe for the complete reversible cycle is zero.
Statement II: The entropy change of the system during the isothermal expansion step is positive.
Statement III: The entropy change of the system during the adiabatic compression step is negative.
Statement IV: The net entropy change of the system for the complete cycle is zero.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct: For any reversible process, the total entropy change of the universe (system + surroundings) is always zero.

Statement II is correct: During isothermal expansion, the gas absorbs heat reversibly ($q_{\text{rev}} > 0$). Since $\Delta S = \dfrac{q_{\text{rev}}}{T}$, the entropy change of the system is positive.

Statement III is incorrect: A reversible adiabatic process involves no heat exchange ($q_{\text{rev}} = 0$). Therefore, the entropy change of the system is zero ($\Delta S = 0$), not negative. It is an isentropic process.

Statement IV is correct: Entropy is a state function. For any complete cycle, the system returns to its initial state, so the net change in entropy of the system is zero.

Thus, exactly three statements (I, II, and IV) are correct.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
During the reversible isothermal compression of one mole of an ideal gas at $300 \text{ K}$, the work done on the gas is $5744 \text{ J}$. What is the ratio of its final volume to its initial volume $\left(\dfrac{V_f}{V_i}\right)$?
(Given: $2.303 \times R \times 300 = 5744 \text{ J}$)
questions.solution:
For a reversible isothermal process, the work done is given by:
$W = -2.303 nRT \log\left(\dfrac{V_f}{V_i}\right)$

Since work is done on the gas (compression), $W$ is positive according to IUPAC sign conventions.
$W = +5744 \text{ J}$

Substituting the given values ($n = 1 \text{ mole}$):
$5744 = -1 \times (2.303 \times R \times 300) \times \log\left(\dfrac{V_f}{V_i}\right)$

We are given that $2.303 \times R \times 300 = 5744 \text{ J}$.
$5744 = -5744 \times \log\left(\dfrac{V_f}{V_i}\right)$

$\log\left(\dfrac{V_f}{V_i}\right) = -1$

Taking the antilog on both sides:
$\dfrac{V_f}{V_i} = 10^{-1} = 0.1$

The ratio of the final volume to the initial volume is $0.1$.

Answer: $0.1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which thermodynamic parameter is not a state function?
questions.solution:
$H$ and $U$ are state functions but $W$ and $q$ are not state functions.
From the equation, $\Delta H=\Delta U+\Delta P V$ 
At constant pressure, $\Delta H=\Delta U+P \Delta V$ 
At constant volume, $\Delta H=\Delta U+V \Delta P$ 
At constant pressure, $\Delta P=0, \Delta H=q_p$
so, it is a state function.
At constant volume, $\Delta V=0, \Delta U=q_v$ so, it is a state function.
Work done in any adiabatic process is state function.
$\Delta U=q-W \quad(\because q=0)$
$\Delta U=-W$
Work done in isothermal process is not a state function.
$W=-q \quad(\because \Delta T=0, q \neq 0)$

questions.q: $\mathrm{CaO}$ and $\mathrm{NaCl}$ have the same crystal structure and approximately the same ionic radii. If $U$ is the lattice energy of $\mathrm{NaCl}$, the approximate lattice energy of $\mathrm{CaO}$ is
questions.solution: $\text{ Lattice energy }=-\frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}$where $q_1$ and $q_2$ are charges on ions and $r$ is the distance between them. Since interionic distances in $\mathrm{CaO}$ and $\mathrm{NaCl}$ are similar, (larger cation has smaller anion and vice versa) therefore, $r$ is almost the same. Therefore, lattice energy depends only on charge. Since the magnitude of charge on $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ions is unity and that on $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\mathrmO^{2-}$ ions is 2 each, therefore, the lattice energy of $\mathrm{CaO}$ is four times the lattice energy of $\mathrm{NaCl}$, i.e., $4 U$.

questions.solution:
The entropy change for a process, when $T$ and $P$ are the variables is given by
$\Delta S=C_P \ln \frac{T_2}{T_1}-R \ln \frac{P_2}{P_1}$

$C_P \ln \frac{T_2}{T_1}=\Delta S$
or $\Delta S=2.303 C_P \log \frac{T_2}{T_1}$.

Heat of neutralization $(\Delta H)=57 \mathrm{~kJ}$, mole of $\mathrm{HNO}_3=0.5$ mole and mole of $\mathrm{NaOH}=0.2$ mole. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion : During an adiabatic process, heat energy is not exchanged between system and its surroundings.
Reason : The temperature of a gas increases when it undergoes an adiabatic expansion.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
In adiabatic process, no heat enters or leaves the system. The system is completely insulated from its surroundings. From first law of thermodynamics, change in internal energy,

\Delta E=q-W=0-W=-W .

Since the work is done at the expense of internal energy, therefore internal energy of the system decreases and hence temperature of the gas falls.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is always feasible?
options: $\Delta H$ (-ve), $T \Delta S$ (+ve) and $\Delta H < T \Delta S$
questions.solution:
Feasibility of reaction is determined by free energy change value $(\Delta G) . \Delta G$ is given by Gibbs - Helmholtz equation :

\Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S

Reaction is feasible if $\Delta G$ value is negative. Therefore, if $\Delta H$ is negative and $T \Delta S$ is positive then the $\Delta G$ will always be feasible.

Key Idea $\gamma=\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}} / \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}$ where, $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}$ are heat capacities at constant pressure and volume, respectively.
For monoatomic gas, $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}}=5 \mathrm{cal}, \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}=3 \mathrm{cal}$
$\gamma=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}}=\frac{5}{3}=1.67$
For diatomic gas, $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}}=7 \mathrm{cal}, \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}=5 \mathrm{cal}$
$_{\mathrm{V}}=6 \mathrm{cal}$
$\gamma=\frac{C_P}{C_V}=\frac{8}{6}=1.33$

At $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, one mole of an ideal gas is compressed isothermally and reversibly from a pressure of 2 atm to 10 atm .
Choose the correct option from the following.

questions.solution:
Work done in isothermal reversible process is
$w=-2.303 n R T \log _{10} \frac{p_1}{p_2}$

$\begin{aligned} n & =1, R=2 \mathrm{cal} \mathrm{K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\ T & =(27+273) \mathrm{K}=300 \mathrm{~K} \\ p_1 & =2 \mathrm{~atm}, p_2=10 \mathrm{~atm}\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad w & =-2.303 \times 1 \times 2 \times 300 \log _{10} \frac{2}{10} \\ w & =+965.54 \mathrm{cal}\end{aligned}$

Now, from first law of thermodynamics,
$\begin{aligned} & q=\Delta U-W=0-965.84 \mathrm{cal} \\ & q=-965.84 \mathrm{cal}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A hypothetical reaction $A \longrightarrow 2 B$ proceeds through the following sequence of steps
I. $A \longrightarrow C ; \Delta_r H=q_1$
II. $C \longrightarrow D ; \Delta_r H=q_2$
III. $\frac{1}{2} D \longrightarrow B ; \Delta_r H=q_3$
The heat of hypothetical reaction is
questions.solution:
One mole of $A$ as reactant So, we write down equation
(i) Two moles of $B$ as product, so we multiply equation (iii) by (b). Finally, we add the three equation term-by-term
$\begin{array}{ll}A \longrightarrow C & q_1 \\ C \longrightarrow D & q_2 \\ D \longrightarrow 2 B & 2 q_3 \\ A \longrightarrow 2 B & q_1+q_2+2 q_3\end{array}$
Therefore, the heat of hypothetical reaction is $q_1+q_2+2 q_3$.

questions.q:
What would be the heat released when an aqueous solution containing 0.5 mole of $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ is mixed with 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$?
(enthalpy of neutralisation is -57.1 kJ )
questions.solution: 0.5 mole of $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ equivalents to 0.5 mole of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$. But only 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ions are available. Thus, 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions will combine with 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ions to form 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ and 0.2 mole of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions will remain unreacted. Heat evolved when 1 mole of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions combine with 1 mole of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ions $=57.1 \mathrm{~kJ}$. Therefore, heat evolved wher 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions combine with 0.3 mole of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ions $=0.3 \times 57.1=17.13 \mathrm{~kJ}$.

questions.q:
The entropy values (in $\mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ ) of $\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})=130.6, \quad \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{~g})=223.0 \quad$ and $\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})=186.7$ at 298 K and 1 atm pressure. Then entropy change for the reaction :
$\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})$ is :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \Delta S^{\circ} & =2 S^{\circ}{ }_{\mathrm{HCl}}-\left(S_{\mathrm{H}_2}^{\circ}+S^{\circ}{ }_{\mathrm{Cl}_2}\right) \\ & =2 \times 186.7-(130.6+223.0) \\ & =19.8 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\mathrm{C}_{\text{(dia) }}+\mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2 ; \Delta H=-395.4 \mathrm{ kJ} / \mathrm{mole} $$\mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{gr}$$)}+$$\mathrm{O}_2$$ \longrightarrow $$\mathrm{CO}_2$$ ; \Delta H=-393.5 $$\mathrm{ kJ}$$ / $$\mathrm{mole} \mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{gr}$)} \longrightarrow $\mathrm{C}_{\text{(dia) }$} ; \Delta H=$ ?$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C}($ dia $)+\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2(\Delta \mathrm{H}=-395.4 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mole})$...(1)
$\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{gr})+\mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2(\Delta \mathrm{H}=-393.5 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mole})$...(2)
subtracting eq. (1) from (2), we have
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{gr}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}_{\text{(dia) }} ; \\ & \begin{aligned}(\Delta \mathrm{H} & =+1.9 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mole}) \\ & \quad[\because \Delta \mathrm{H}=-393.5-(-395.4) \\ & \left.=+1.9 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right]\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In an isothermal process
questions.solution:
the temperature is constant.
So, $\quad \Delta E=0$
Hence $\Delta H=P \Delta V$ (As, $\Delta H=\Delta E+P \Delta V$ )
$\Delta H=W$ $\qquad (\because W=P \Delta V)$
